tagline: Innovating medicines and vaccines to advance human health globally.
hero_kpi_rationale: Merck invests heavily in R&D to develop new medicines and vaccines, a key driver of its future growth and leadership position in the pharmaceutical sector.

kpis.name: Research and development
kpis.explanation: Expenses dedicated to the research and development of new products and technologies.
kpis.description: R&D expenses decreased by 12% in 2025 compared to 2024, falling from $17.9 billion to $15.8 billion. This decline resulted from the absence of significant IPR&D charges comparable to those in 2024.
kpis.signal: Sharp decline in R&D expenses in 2025, primarily due to amortization adjustments following acquisitions and restructurings.

kpis.name: Sales
kpis.explanation: Total revenue generated from the sale of goods and services.
kpis.description: Sales increased by 1.3% in 2025, reaching $65.0 billion, compared to $64.2 billion in 2024.
kpis.signal: Modest sales growth, indicating market stability and resilience against competitive pressures.

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Profit remaining after deduction of all expenses, including taxes.
kpis.description: Net income increased by 6.6% in 2025, reaching $18.3 billion, reflecting effective cost management and improved operational performance.
kpis.signal: Significant increase in net income, suggesting improved profitability despite strategic acquisitions.

kpis.name: Cost of sales
kpis.explanation: Direct cost of goods sold by the company.
kpis.description: Cost of sales increased by 7.8% in 2025, reaching $16.4 billion, outpacing revenue growth and slightly reducing gross margins.
kpis.signal: Cost of sales growth exceeding sales growth, reflecting inflationary pressures on production costs.

kpis.name: Selling, general and administrative
kpis.explanation: Expenses related to sales, marketing, administration, and general overhead.
kpis.description: These expenses decreased by 0.7% in 2025 to $10.7 billion, demonstrating control over administrative spending.
kpis.signal: Slight decrease in selling, general and administrative expenses, indicating effective cost management and operational discipline.

kpis.name: Capital expenditures
kpis.explanation: Investments in tangible assets such as plants and equipment.
kpis.description: Capital expenditures increased by 21.9% in 2025, reaching $4.1 billion, supporting future growth and manufacturing facility upgrades.
kpis.signal: Significant increase in capital expenditures, reflecting expansion of production capacity and technological modernization.

kpis.name: Total current assets
kpis.explanation: Assets expected to be converted into cash or consumed within one year.
kpis.description: Current assets increased by 12.2% in 2025 to $43.5 billion, reflecting improved cash position and higher inventory levels.
kpis.signal: Strong growth in current assets, indicating improved liquidity and increased accounts receivable following acquisitions.

kpis.name: Total current liabilities
kpis.explanation: Debts and obligations due within one year.
kpis.description: Current liabilities remained stable in 2025 at $28.3 billion, demonstrating a healthy balance sheet structure.
kpis.signal: Stability in current liabilities, suggesting balanced management of short-term obligations and sound financial discipline.

kpis.name: Long-Term Debt
kpis.explanation: Debts and borrowings with maturities exceeding one year.
kpis.description: Long-term debt increased sharply by 35.6% in 2025, reaching $46.8 billion, to finance strategic acquisitions aimed at strengthening the product portfolio.
kpis.signal: Significant increase in long-term debt, justified by financing major acquisitions including Prometheus Biosciences ($10.7 billion) and others.

kpis.name: Acquisition of Cidara
kpis.explanation: Acquisition of a biotechnology company for $9.2 billion to strengthen the antiviral portfolio with MK-1406, a long-acting candidate for influenza prevention.
kpis.description: In January 2026, Merck acquired Cidara for $9.2 billion, including payments for shares and stock options. The primary asset is MK-1406, a long-acting antiviral therapeutic candidate in clinical evaluation.
kpis.signal: Major strategic acquisition to develop innovative antiviral treatments for seasonal and pandemic influenza.

kpis.name: Acquisition of Prometheus Biosciences
kpis.explanation: Acquisition for $10.7 billion to strengthen the immunology and inflammatory diseases portfolio.
kpis.description: The acquisition of Prometheus Biosciences, completed in 2025, cost $10.7 billion (net of cash acquired), according to Cash Flow Statement data. This acquisition strengthens Merck's position in immunology.
kpis.signal: Significant acquisition completed in 2025 to expand presence in immunology and inflammatory gastrointestinal diseases.

kpis.short: Research and development charge for acquired IPR&D
kpis.name: Research and development charge for acquired IPR&D
kpis.explanation: One-time charge of $9.0 billion recorded in Q1 2026 for acquired research and development assets (IPR&D) with no alternative future use, as part of the Cidara acquisition.
kpis.description: A charge of approximately $9.0 billion will be recorded in the first quarter of 2026 for acquired R&D assets (IPR&D) with no alternative future use, in accordance with accounting standards for asset acquisitions.
kpis.signal: Major one-time charge related to the Cidara acquisition, impacting Q1 2026 R&D results by approximately $3.65 per share.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Montant total versé en dividendes par action sur l'année fiscale. Indicateur clé pour les investisseurs orientés revenus.
kpis.description: 5-year history of declared dividends per share (2021-2025).

kpis.name: Capital Returned to Shareholders
kpis.explanation: Total annuel du cash redistribué aux actionnaires : dividendes versés + rachats d'actions (treasury stock).
kpis.description: For 2025: cumulative dividends + share buybacks in billions USD.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Part du bénéfice net redistribuée en dividendes. Au-dessus de 80 % indique un dividende potentiellement non-soutenable.
kpis.description: Dividends / net income for 2025 (based on net income attributable to shareholders).

risks.title: Regulatory Risk
risks.score_rationale: The pharmaceutical sector is subject to strict government and international regulations for drug approval and commercialization. Non-compliance could result in rejected approvals, substantial fines, or market withdrawals.

risks.title: Increased Competition
risks.score_rationale: The pharmaceutical market is highly competitive, with biosimilars and generics threatening existing products. Increased competition could reduce market share and profit margins.

risks.title: Credit and Interest Rate Risk
risks.score_rationale: With long-term debt of $46.8 billion (up 35.6%), Merck is exposed to interest rate fluctuations. A significant rise in rates could increase debt servicing costs and reduce available cash flows.

risks.title: Pharmaceutical Pricing Risk
risks.score_rationale: Governments and reimbursement agencies are exerting increasing pressure on drug prices, particularly in the United States and Europe, potentially affecting revenues.

ai_positioning.summary: No significant mention of artificial intelligence, machine learning, or related technologies was found in MRK's 10-K filing.
